messages.subject: measurementInvariance with lavaan
parts:
I have a (hopefully) quick question about testing measurementInvariance() with lavaan.  I'm running a correlated factors model that is comparing 2 groups, and the change in CFI values is very small, until the test of strict invariance (significant chi-square, and delta CFI > .01).  This test is of constraining the residual variances across groups.

When I look at the modificationIndices() on this model, the largest MI pertains to the variance of a particular item (e.g., X33 ~~ X33).  I put that into the partial.group argument and reran the model, which has improved fit.

Running modificationIndices() on the new model, the largest MI pertains to a residual covariance between two items (e.g., X33 ~~ X45).  However, if I put that into partial.group, nothing happens (X33 ~~ X45 is still listed as the largest MI for the resulting model).  I realize that there isn't a covariance for exogenous variables portion of the output, so perhaps I should be approaching this modification differently?

For a reproducible example, this is similar to what I'm working with (barring the fact that this dataset has other invariance issues):

library("lavaan")
library("semTools")


HW.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '


out1 <- measurementInvariance(HW.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, strict = TRUE)


SW_strict <- out1$fit.residuals
summary(SW_strict)
SW_mods <- modificationIndices(SW_strict)  # pretend largest residual is x6 ~~ x6


out2 <- measurementInvariance(HW.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school", strict = TRUE,
                              group.partial = c("x6 ~~ x6"))


SW_partial1 <- out2$fit.residuals
summary(SW_partial1)  # variance of x6 is now free across groups


# Modification Indices
SW_p_mods1 <- modificationIndices(SW_partial1)
SW_p_mods1 <- SW_p_mods1[order(SW_p_mods1$mi, decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(SW_p_mods1[SW_p_mods1$op == "~~",])      # largest MI is x2 ~~ x7


out3 <- measurementInvariance(HW.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school", strict = TRUE,
                              group.partial = c("x6 ~~ x6", "x2 ~~ x7"))

# The fit of out2$fit.residuals and out3$fit.residuals is the same.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance with lavaan
parts:
Strict invariance only constrains residual variances across groups, not residual covariances.  That residual covariance probably wasn't even a free parameter in your model (fixed to zero by default), so you just need to add it to your syntax.

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance with lavaan
parts:
On 03/23/2015 04:49 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> Strict invariance only constrains residual variances across groups, not
> residual covariances. That residual covariance probably wasn't even a
> free parameter in your model (fixed to zero by default), so you just
> need to add it to your syntax.

Indeed.

In this setting, I would avoid using the measurementInvariance()
function, and fit the individual (configure/weak/strong/...) models
yourself, by using labels to constrain (or free) the parameters across
groups.

This gives you must more flexibility.

Yves.
